answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation costly to mirror. New agents begin in a harbor of low-value, independently verifiable tasks, with part of every payment held as a refundable bond that is slashed on proven fraud. An attacker running a raven flock of fake identities must fund a bond and finish real work for each one before reaching high-value jobs, so faking scale costs linearly while an honest agent graduates once and keeps its record.
